content:
STAGE: evidence read (goal: ground the ranking in the frozen bundles before scoring)
READ: the four frozen bundles in the prompt (2ec8dfb2, 69fae840, 7d383ca4, e07e5e86) plus the five-part scope contract and the one-run/no-ablation policy. The workspace contains only session/progress/log files, so the prompt bundles are the whole evidence record.
OBSERVED: all four bundles share the same OBSERVED block E4-E11. E6 (width-20 beam survival) is the only behavioural recall evidence: l1_br 0.04671, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363, successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500; gold prefix alive at depth 2 is 0.829 for l1_br_euclid and 0.161 for l1_br. E7: l1_br T1/T2/T3 NLL 0.00 and T4 9.03; l1_br_euclid 3.22/4.36/1.23; the geodesic variants carry T1 NLL 2.3-2.5. E8: pair cluster-sharing 0.3106 at K=16 falling to 0.0822 at K=256. E5: successor entropy 0.93-3.41 with top1 mass 0.438->0.054. E11: same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067.
REASONING: the curvature-profile forensic numbers (+0.26/-0.16/-0.20, p=0.0095) used in every motivation are NOT in the bundle - E12/E13 are PROPOSED, not OBSERVED. So every proposal rests on an unmeasured premise, and the only OBSERVED geometry evidence says heavy hyperbolic transport chains (0.0546-0.0550) lost to the Euclidean level-1 quantizer (0.06207-0.06233) and that capacity at K=256 is the binding constraint (0.0822). Ranking therefore turns on (a) whether the geometry changes the residual chain or only a small number of metric scalars, (b) spec completeness, (c) collapse risk against the E8/E6 capacity evidence.
OPEN: no ablation arms are run, so mechanical soundness and boundedness of the perturbation are the only discriminators available.

STAGE: per-proposal scope-and-risk assessment (goal: place each proposal against the sparingly-observed evidence)
READ: the four SPECIFICATION blocks, COST blocks, HYPOTHESIS blocks and RISKS lists.
OBSERVED: (1) nullcurv-hinge-rq: fully specified equations for d_L,c, exp/log at origin, per-level trainable c_l, hinge max(0,k1-k2)^2+max(0,k2-k3)^2, null of 10 histograms-preserving shuffles every 250 epochs, sigma floor 0.05|mu|, lambda = L_RQ(0)/max(L_curv(0),1e-6) derived at init, decoder still consumes tangent vectors so Stage-3 is untouched; guard on level-3 usage >=0.9x epoch-0. (2) CURVALLOC: c_l = c0 exp(-delta_l), rho_l = rho0 exp(delta_l/2), delta mean-zero clipped +-1, EMA 0.5, 15 refreshes, stop-gradient; cost quoted at B=256 not the frozen 1023. (3) CURVPROF: cost and safeguards given but no equation is ever given for c_l - the text says "quotient and curvature are computed as below" and "m comes from the measured spread" without defining either; it changes the Mobius log/geodesic step of the prefix chain at levels 2-3. (4) ORC: Poincare distance d_k=(2/sqrt k) artanh(...) with a per-code k, k in [k0/4,4k0], so the argmin compares numbers produced under different metrics; 600 refreshes on a 4096-item subsample plus a one-off rank-128 SVD + k-means reference partition.
REASONING: nullcurv is the only one where the curved quantity is also the trained quantity on one differentiable path, and it confines the behavioural perturbation to 3 scalars while leaving the Euclidean decoder and the prefix chain intact. CURVALLOC is also 3-scalar and bounded but its curvature->space mapping and the rho exponent are asserted, not derived, and the feedback is a stop-gradient schedule. CURVPROF leaves the central map undefined and is the closest in form to the transport variants that E6/E7 show underperforming. ORC's per-code metric makes the nearest-code rule ill-defined (smaller k systematically yields smaller distances), which drives assignment toward one clip end and reproduces exactly the usage collapse that E8 (0.0822 pair sharing at K=256) and E6 (l1_br 0.04671 with a degenerate prefix) warn about.
OPEN: all four depend on an unmeasured curvature-profile premise; a single-run null cannot separate a wrong target from a weak surrogate.

STAGE: final ranking (goal: one position per proposal, grounded)
OBSERVED/READ: E6, E7, E8, E5, E11 of the frozen bundles; the four SPECIFICATION blocks.
CONCLUSION: position 1 nullcurv-hinge-rq, 2 CURVALLOC-LORENTZ-RQ, 3 CURVPROF-TRANSPORT-RQ, 4 ORC-CELLCHART.
REASONING: nullcurv is the only proposal whose curvature is both trained by the behavioural statistic and used as the assignment metric on a single differentiable path, it is the only one with a complete equation set and a derived coupling weight, and it changes the partition with 3 scalars while keeping the Euclidean decoder, which is the least exposure to the E6/E7 result that geometric transport chains score 0.0546-0.0550 against 0.06207-0.06233 for the Euclidean level-1 quantizer, and to the E8 capacity ceiling 0.0822 at K=256. CURVALLOC is second because it is also only 3 per-level scalars and clipped/EMA-bounded, but its curvature sign, radial exponent and stop-gradient schedule are asserted rather than derived and its cost is quoted at B=256 not the frozen 1023. CURVPROF is third because it never specifies the map from the standardised profile to c_l (the one quantity the whole mechanism needs) and it rewrites the Mobius transport of the residual chain, the family E6/E7 shows underperforming. ORC is fourth because comparing d_k under a different k per code is not a well-defined nearest-code rule, the smaller-k codes win systematically, and that reproduces the usage-collapse pattern E6/E8 flag, on top of 600 noisy 4096-item refreshes and an extra SVD+k-means reference partition.
OPEN: the curvature-profile forensic premise (+0.26/-0.16/-0.20) is not in any bundle (E12/E13 are PROPOSED); this caps confidence in all four equally and is not itself a discriminator.
